primary_sources: Clean Code by Robert C. Martin
Gang of Four Design Patterns Standards

rules.rule_name: Meaningful Names and Small Single-Responsibility Functions
rules.explanation: Writing monolithic functions with cryptic variable names makes codebases unreadable, fragile, and difficult to maintain.
rules.do: Use intention-revealing, searchable names for variables and functions, and keep functions small with a single, well-defined responsibility.
rules.dont: Do not write multi-page functions that perform multiple unrelated tasks or use single-letter variable names outside of standard loop counters.

rules.rule_name: SOLID Principles of Object-Oriented and Component Design
rules.explanation: Tight coupling and rigid class hierarchies violate architectural scalability, making every small feature addition break existing modules.
rules.do: Enforce SOLID principles (Single Responsibility, Open/Closed, Liskov Substitution, Interface Segregation, Dependency Inversion) across all software components.
rules.dont: Do not tightly couple high-level business logic directly to low-level implementation details or concrete drivers.

rules.explanation: Reinventing custom architectural solutions for standard software problems leads to messy, inconsistent code structures.
rules.do: Apply established Gang of Four (GoF) design patterns (e.g., Factory, Singleton, Strategy, Observer) where appropriate to solve recurring architectural challenges.
rules.dont: Do not overuse or force complex design patterns where simple, straightforward code structures are more effective.

rules.rule_name: Boy Scout Rule and Continuous Code Refactoring
rules.explanation: Leaving messy code untouched ('technical debt accumulation') progressively degrades code quality until the entire system requires a rewrite.
rules.do: Apply the Boy Scout Rule: leave the code cleaner than you found it by continuously refactoring small structural smells during regular feature development.
rules.dont: Do not ignore code smells, duplicated code blocks, or dead commented-out sections in files you modify.
